payload.title: Closed-Loop Multiplicity Calibration for Additive Count Mass
plain_method_steps: Read only physically separated, feature-only supplied pose tracks and retain the supplied identity slots solely for routing.

Construct deterministic synthetic motion atoms from short pose segments followed by a smooth return path; repeat each atom one to four times under disclosed crop, masking, and monotone-resampling transforms.

Train a compact temporal filter to emit nonnegative interval count mass, using the known synthetic multiplicity for absolute calibration and cut-additivity and transformed-view consistency as auxiliary constraints.
At inference, sum interval mass once per supplied identity; expose transformation disagreement as a failure score rather than selecting a period.
payload.core_hypothesis: Known multiplicity of synthetic closed pose loops can calibrate an additive event-mass measure that transfers to real repetitions without learner access to real per-person count, density, period, or boundary labels.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: Using only checksum-frozen feature-only train/validation tracks, freeze a held-out synthetic-loop pack before fitting. Kill if multiplicity MAE over one-to-four repeats exceeds 0.15 cycles, median random-cut additivity error exceeds 5%, or time-shuffled non-loop controls receive more than 0.25 median count mass. Evaluator labels remain unopened.
payload.expected_contribution: A bounded study of selector-free absolute count calibration through synthetic loop multiplicity and measure additivity on supplied pose tracks; synthetic correspondence supervision and external pose/tracker supervision would be disclosed.
payload.risk: Synthetic return paths may be too unlike semantic repetitions, and the learner may recognize construction seams instead of transferable motion closure.
closest_prior_boundary: RepNet already uses synthetic repetitions; synthetic repetition construction is not a contribution by itself.
PAMS already covers self-supervised skeleton periodic learning and localized tempo perturbations; the boundary is additive count-mass calibration without a pseudo-period selector.
MultiCounter+ already establishes robust identity-indexed MRAC and external detection/tracking machinery.
DeepPhase already occupies unsupervised motion phase, while TWCRAC occupies local cycle-consistency territory; neither phase learning nor local consistency is claimed.

payload.title: Band-Marginalized Limb-Phase Synchronization
plain_method_steps: Transform root-centered joint velocities with a fixed complex wavelet bank spanning the admissible temporal scales, retaining every band rather than selecting a period.
Create a confidence-weighted graph whose nodes are limb-band analytic phases and whose edges encode stable phase offsets, including allowed anti-phase relations.
Solve an SO(2) synchronization problem per window, then marginalize angular current across bands according to graph residuals instead of choosing one spectral peak.
Integrate the reliable consensus current per supplied identity and emit an abstention flag when graph connectivity, circular concentration, or cross-band agreement is inadequate.
payload.core_hypothesis: Repetitive motion produces mutually consistent phase currents across several limbs even when any single limb or frequency band locks to a half or double harmonic; marginal synchronization can therefore count more reliably than a hard period selector.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: On a newly specified, immutable pose-only diagnostic pack derived from frozen train/validation feature distributions, test chirps, pauses, anti-phase limbs, half/double harmonics, missing joints, and nonperiodic distractors. Kill if median winding error exceeds 10%, harmonic locking exceeds 5%, or the failure flag detects fewer than 80% of ambiguous cases at 10% false alarms. This pack must not modify or reinterpret the killed WARP-PHASE fixtures.
payload.expected_contribution: A selector-free multichannel signal-fusion hypothesis for supplied-track repetition counting, with an explicit reliability output based on circular synchronization residuals.
payload.risk: Limb phases can be weak, intermittent, or genuinely multi-rate, causing cancellation or confident synchronization to a nonsemantic motion component.
closest_prior_boundary: DeepPhase already learns local multichannel motion phase; the possible distinction is fixed-band cross-limb synchronization and reliability, not unsupervised phase itself.
PAMS already uses period-adaptive multiscale consistency and inference consensus; marginal graph synchronization must be compared directly and not described as the first multiscale pose method.
TWCRAC already covers local cycle consistency and nonstationary motion; no local-window or dynamic-tempo novelty claim is permitted.
MultiCounter+ already covers identity-indexed variable-period MRAC; supplied tracking remains external supervision.

payload.title: Conditioned Hankel Pole-Path Posterior
plain_method_steps: Form confidence-masked multichannel block-Hankel matrices from each supplied identity's normalized pose velocities.
Use total-least-squares matrix pencils to estimate damped complex poles and attach rank-gap, residual, and condition-number diagnostics to every pole.
Link compatible poles across overlapping windows with a bounded dynamic program and represent fundamentals and integer-related harmonics as a posterior family rather than a single selected period.
Integrate posterior expected angular frequency to obtain a continuous count and widen or abstain when the subspace is ill-conditioned or competing paths remain unresolved.
payload.core_hypothesis: A low-rank pole model can track nonstationary repetition rates while exposing mathematical non-identifiability, allowing harmonic ambiguity to become reported uncertainty instead of a brittle hard decision.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: Run a CPU-only frozen diagnostic suite containing pose-shaped damped oscillations, smooth and abrupt chirps, harmonic mixtures, missing samples, and matched aperiodic motion. Kill if well-conditioned cases exceed 10% integrated-count error, fewer than 85% of deliberately ill-conditioned cases are flagged, or perturbing valid pose coordinates within the frozen noise envelope changes count by more than 10%.
payload.expected_contribution: A failure-aware subspace signal-processing baseline for per-identity supplied-track counting, emphasizing pole-path uncertainty rather than learned period supervision.
payload.risk: Human motion may violate the short-window low-rank oscillator model, and matrix-pencil estimates can be unstable under severe missingness or closely spaced modes.
closest_prior_boundary: Runia et al. and RepNet already establish nonstationary spectral or time-varying-period estimation; spectral estimation itself is not claimed.
PAMS already covers multiscale pose periodic learning, and DeepPhase already covers local motion-phase manifolds.
TWCRAC's local nonstationary formulation remains an unresolved boundary, so the claim must stay at conditioned pole tracking and abstention.
MultiCounter+ supplies the MRAC task boundary; this candidate neither detects nor tracks people.

payload.title: Leave-One-Person-Out Common-Mode Cancellation
plain_method_steps: Align all supplied person tracks on their frozen source-frame clock and compute confidence-masked root-centered pose velocities.
For each target identity, estimate a robust low-rank common-motion subspace from the other identities only, with explicit guards for one-person scenes and insufficient overlap.
Subtract only the component that is coherent across multiple people and joint groups, then pass the residual and untouched target signal through the same frozen label-restricted counter.
Report nuisance attenuation, target-signal preservation, and changes in untouched identities; never feed person identifiers or evaluator labels to the model.
payload.core_hypothesis: Camera motion and scene-wide nuisance often occupy a cross-person common subspace, while true repetition evidence remains identity-specific; leave-one-person-out cancellation can improve counting without erasing the target's motion.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: On frozen feature-only train/validation tracks, inject checksum-frozen shared translation, scale, and low-frequency camera trajectories plus independent person-specific oscillations. Kill if common nuisance is attenuated by less than 15 dB, target oscillatory energy preservation falls below 90%, or changing one person's trajectory alters another person's residual by more than 1%.
payload.expected_contribution: A multi-person signal-separation study linking robust common-mode rejection to supplied-track repetition counting and cross-person interference diagnostics.
payload.risk: People may intentionally move synchronously, so genuine action energy can enter the common subspace; many videos may also contain too few overlapping identities for stable decomposition.
closest_prior_boundary: MultiCounter+ already uses spatial-temporal consistency and identity-indexed MRAC; cross-person common-mode cancellation must not be framed as identity-consistency novelty.
PAMS supplies a strong pose-periodic downstream baseline; any benefit must be isolated to the nuisance-removal front end.
DeepPhase is not displaced because this candidate does not claim a new phase representation.
TWCRAC's local periodic statistics are separate; no dynamic-threshold or local-cycle claim is made.

payload.title: Fragment-Boundary Transport for Count-Mass Conservation
plain_method_steps: Freeze a label-restricted supplied-track base response model and treat its architecture and periodic representation as non-contributions.
Create deterministic feature-only cuts, gaps, and re-entry patterns from each complete training track while preserving the supplied identity routing key.

Learn a small boundary transport operator from endpoint pose and velocity states so that intact response mass equals fragment mass plus an explicit boundary correction; use wrong-identity endpoint pairings as negatives.
At inference, compose fragment masses only when the transport residual is small and otherwise emit an abstention or interval rather than silently joining them.
payload.core_hypothesis: Most fragmentation error is localized at missing boundaries and can be represented as a transport correction between endpoint motion states, enabling count-mass conservation without real count or period labels.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: Using frozen feature-only train/validation tracks and predeclared cut patterns, kill if unseen-cut reconstruction error exceeds 5% of intact response mass, wrong-identity pairings receive more than 10% of correct boundary weight, the endpoint code collapses below a frozen effective-rank floor, or one-person cuts alter byte-identical untouched-person outputs.
payload.expected_contribution: A failure-aware, supplied-track fragmentation mechanism and conservation diagnostic; the base counter, supplied identities, and external tracking supervision remain explicitly attributed.
payload.risk: A self-consistency objective can preserve a biased base counter, while long gaps or large tempo changes may make boundary correction fundamentally unidentifiable.
closest_prior_boundary: MultiCounter+ already addresses tracking and temporal consistency; this candidate is not a tracking or re-identification contribution.
PAMS and DeepPhase may instantiate the frozen base response, but their periodic representations are not claimed.
TWCRAC already covers time-window-cycle consistency, so the residual claim is boundary transport under synthetic fragmentation rather than window consistency.
Any later predicted-track study would require separate tracking metrics; this bounded candidate remains supplied-track only.

payload.title: Persistent-Cohomology Crossing Ensemble
plain_method_steps: Build delay embeddings of confidence-masked pose velocities separately for each supplied identity and several fixed joint subsets.
Compute persistent one-dimensional cohomology and derive circular coordinates only for loops whose persistence and neighborhood support pass frozen numerical checks.
Count signed crossings through an ensemble of data-derived Poincare sections, then aggregate section counts with a median and expose section disagreement as uncertainty.
Use no learned period, count, density, or cycle-boundary label; tracks without a persistent loop receive an abstention rather than a forced count.
payload.core_hypothesis: A genuine repetitive action traces a stable loop in delay-embedded pose space, so topological winding and section-crossing agreement can count repetitions without selecting a temporal period and can fail visibly on non-loop motion.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: On deterministic synthetic loops embedded in frozen train/validation pose noise and on pose-only time-warp, reversal, crop, and shuffled-time controls, kill if median crossing error exceeds 0.25 cycles, monotone resampling changes winding by more than 2%, shuffled-time false loops exceed 5%, or fewer than 80% of deliberately non-loop tracks abstain.
payload.expected_contribution: A selector-free topological counting hypothesis with an explicit identifiability certificate for supplied pose tracks.
payload.risk: Real actions can form open, self-intersecting, drifting, or multi-loop trajectories; persistent topology may also be computationally heavy and sensitive to embedding choices.
closest_prior_boundary: DeepPhase already occupies unsupervised local motion-phase manifolds; the narrow distinction is persistent-loop crossing with an abstention certificate, not phase discovery.
PAMS already covers self-supervised skeleton periodic representation and tempo robustness; identical supplied-track comparisons are required.
TWCRAC already covers local cycles and nonstationarity; no first-cycle or local-window claim is permitted.
MultiCounter+ establishes per-person MRAC, while the supplied pose/tracker pipeline remains external supervision.

payload.title: Set-Valued Counting Under Pose Missingness
plain_method_steps: Estimate train-only kinematic uncertainty sets from feature-side bone-length and velocity statistics, without opening evaluator labels.
Propagate observed joints and missing-coordinate intervals through a fixed multiband analytic-response bank to obtain lower and upper interval response mass.

Aggregate interval mass once per supplied identity, preserving inclusion under nested missingness masks and returning a count interval plus a point estimate only when the interval is sufficiently narrow.
Keep externally supervised pose and tracking explicit, and evaluate missingness severity and interval width separately from count accuracy.
payload.core_hypothesis: For incomplete pose, a defensible interval of repetition counts is more scientifically reliable than imputation followed by an overconfident point count, and useful bounds can be obtained from kinematic uncertainty without per-person labels.
payload.cheap_kill_gate: Apply nested deterministic masks to frozen feature-only train/validation tracks. Kill if interval nesting is violated in any audited case, the unmasked estimate is contained in fewer than 95% of masked intervals, median width exceeds 1.5 cycles at 30% missing joints, or width fails to increase monotonically with missingness. No evaluator label is needed for this gate.
payload.expected_contribution: A failure-aware partial-identification protocol and signal-processing construction for supplied-track repetition counting under pose dropout, with final validation labels used only after predictions and intervals are frozen.
payload.risk: Valid uncertainty sets may be too wide for practical counting, while empirically tight sets may not cover unobserved motion and could give misleading guarantees.
closest_prior_boundary: SSTRAC and related work already study skeleton repair and occlusion robustness; this candidate claims neither repair nor missing-pose novelty, only set-valued count propagation.
MultiCounter+ already addresses robust MRAC and identity consistency.
PAMS supplies the pose-periodic comparison boundary, and DeepPhase supplies the unsupervised phase boundary.
TWCRAC already covers local nonstationary statistics; dynamic thresholds and local windows are not contributions here.

failure_memory: The signed WARP-PHASE warp-integral candidate is terminally killed by immutable Gate-2 counts 246/55/144/50/66. None of these candidates changes its thresholds, fixtures, selector, semantics, or status, and none is a fallback continuation of that method.

The killed branch has zero eligible efficacy results and no training or server authorization. Engineering fixtures, CPU smokes, and self-consistency gates must never be reported as count-performance evidence.

Any future learner must consume physically separated feature-only train data; evaluator count, density, period, and boundary fields remain in a separately permissioned vault. Frozen validation labels may be joined only after predictions and decisions are frozen.

External detector, GT-box assistance, pose-estimator, tracker, supplied identity tracks, synthetic correspondence or multiplicity, and any video-level supervision must be disclosed. The precise ceiling is that the counting learner uses no real per-person count or period labels.
Forbidden language remains: every variant of first, annotation-free, end-to-end, constant-time, and SOTA without eligible protocol-matched evidence.

MultiCounter and MultiCounter+ already establish MRAC, per-person outputs, identity consistency, and variable-period multi-person counting. PAMS already establishes self-supervised pose periodic learning, multiscale consistency, inference consensus, and localized tempo perturbations. DeepPhase already establishes unsupervised local motion phase. TWCRAC already occupies local-window cycle consistency, dynamic local statistics, and nonstationary motion, with full-method overlap unresolved.

All cheap gates above are new candidate-specific, checksum-frozen train/validation feature diagnostics. They cannot reuse, replace, repair, or reinterpret the immutable WARP-PHASE Gate-2 population, and passing them would authorize only further review rather than a claim.
